For care managers

What to check before you book agency staff.

By Aviteus Healthcare. Checked against official guidance on 25 November 2026.

An agency worker on your floor is working in your service. If something goes wrong, or an inspector asks, you need to know how that person was checked. Here are the questions to ask, and the checks you can make yourself.

The short answer

Before a new agency worker starts, make sure you have confirmed their identity, their right to work, the right level of criminal record check, their references, their training and, for nurses, their NMC registration. Ask the agency for this in writing before the shift.

The checklist

CheckWhat to ask the agencyCan you check it yourself?
1. IdentityWill the worker bring photo ID that matches the profile you sent?Yes. Check the ID on arrival.
2. Right to workHas the right to work check been done, and how?Ask the agency. The business that employs the worker is responsible for this check.
3. Criminal record checkWhat level of check, and when was it issued?Ask for the certificate date and level.
4. ReferencesHow many, from whom, and covering which period?Ask for a summary.
5. TrainingWhich courses, and when do they expire?Ask for dates, not just a list of course names.
6. NMC registration (nurses)What is the nurse's PIN?Yes. Search the public NMC register.
7. Social care registrationIn Wales: is the worker registered with Social Care Wales, or within their first six months? In Northern Ireland: are they registered with NISCC?Yes. Both registers can be searched online.
8. ExperienceHas the worker worked in a setting like yours?Ask at handover.

Criminal record checks: what level?

Most hands-on care roles are in "regulated activity". In England and Wales, that usually means an Enhanced DBS check with a check of the adults' barred list. Eligibility is set in law, so the agency must request the level the role allows.

In Scotland, membership of the Protecting Vulnerable Groups (PVG) scheme has been a legal requirement for people doing regulated roles since 1 April 2025. In Northern Ireland, checks are done through AccessNI, and care roles usually need an enhanced check.

Ask for the date. A criminal record certificate shows information on the day it was issued. Ask whether the worker is on the DBS Update Service, which lets the agency check for new information.

Checking a nurse's registration yourself

The NMC register is public and free to search. Enter the nurse's name or PIN and check three things: the registration is current, it is the right part of the register (adult, mental health or learning disability), and there are no conditions that affect the work you need.

Warning signs

  • The agency cannot tell you who is coming until they arrive
  • Training is listed with no dates
  • No one answers out of hours when you need to raise a problem
  • You are asked to start a worker "and the paperwork will follow"
  • There are no written terms between you and the agency

On the day

  1. Check photo ID against the profile.
  2. Give a short handover: fire exits, emergency procedures, who to ask for help, key risks for the people they will support.
  3. Tell them what they must not do, such as tasks they are not trained for.
  4. Sign the timesheet at the end, and give the agency honest feedback.

Questions

Who does the right to work check for an agency worker?

The business that employs or engages the worker carries out the check. For most temporary agency workers, that is the agency. You can still ask how and when it was done.

Can I ask to see a worker's DBS certificate?

You can ask the agency to confirm the level, date and whether the worker is on the Update Service. Sharing the certificate itself depends on the agency's data protection arrangements with the worker.

Official sources

  • Right to work checks: an employer's guide (Home Office, updated 1 October 2026)
  • DBS eligibility guidance (Disclosure and Barring Service)
  • Protecting Vulnerable Groups (PVG) scheme (mygov.scot)
  • Information for recruitment agencies (Social Care Wales)
  • Apply for an AccessNI check (nidirect)
  • Registration matters (Northern Ireland Social Care Council)
  • Search the NMC register (Nursing and Midwifery Council)

This guide is general information, not legal advice.
